content.value_statement: Flutter widgets can be difficult to inspect without launching the full application. This skill adds isolated previews with appropriate annotations, configurations, and workflows.
actual_capabilities: Adds Preview annotations to eligible Flutter widget functions, static methods, constructors, and factories.
Configures preview names, groups, sizes, themes, and brightness variants.
Creates reusable custom Preview annotations for shared widget settings.
Creates MultiPreview classes for repeated preview combinations.
Guides preview startup and iteration through supported IDEs or the Flutter CLI.
Accounts for web preview constraints involving native APIs, assets, callbacks, and unconstrained widgets.
limitations: Requires a Flutter version and development environment that support the Widget Previewer.
Cannot preview widgets that depend directly or transitively on unsupported native APIs without conditional alternatives.
Requires eligible public targets without required constructor arguments.
Does not replace device testing, integration testing, accessibility testing, or production validation.

use_cases.description: Generate light, dark, and constrained previews for consistent visual review.

use_cases.title: Standardize Package Previews
use_cases.description: Create reusable preview annotations that apply shared themes and wrappers across a component library.

prompt_templates.title: Add a Basic Preview
prompt_templates.prompt: Add a Flutter widget preview for [widget name]. Use a clear preview name and group, then explain the changes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Create the first isolated preview for an eligible widget.

prompt_templates.title: Add Visual Variants
prompt_templates.prompt: Add previews for [widget name] in light and dark modes. Include suitable sizes and preserve existing behavior.
prompt_templates.scenario: Compare one widget across common visual configurations.

prompt_templates.prompt: Create a reusable Preview annotation for widgets in [feature]. Apply the shared theme, wrapper, naming, and grouping requirements.
prompt_templates.scenario: Standardize preview configuration across several widgets.

prompt_templates.title: Design a MultiPreview Matrix
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a MultiPreview setup for [widgets] across [configurations]. Handle web preview limitations, minimize duplication, and provide validation steps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Generate and maintain an advanced preview matrix for a component library.

output_examples.input: Add a preview for the profile summary card in light and dark modes.
output_examples.output: The profile summary card gains two grouped previews with descriptive names and theme-specific brightness settings. Existing widget behavior remains unchanged.

output_examples.input: Create reusable previews for buttons that need the application theme.
output: A custom preview annotation applies the shared application theme.
Button previews use consistent grouping and names.
Validation steps cover IDE discovery and preview refresh behavior.

output_examples.input: Prepare a responsive preview set for the product tile.
output_examples.output: A MultiPreview configuration presents compact and wide product tile variants with explicit constraints and consistent labels.

best_practices: Use descriptive preview names and groups so related components remain easy to find.
Set explicit sizes for widgets that do not receive reliable constraints.
Extract repeated themes, wrappers, and configurations into reusable preview annotations.
anti_patterns: Do not call native APIs from widgets rendered in the web-based preview environment.
Do not use private or nonconstant callbacks in preview annotations.
Do not treat successful preview rendering as complete application testing.

faq.question: Which Flutter elements can receive previews?
faq.answer: Use top-level functions, static methods, or public constructors and factories without required arguments that return supported widget types.

faq.question: How do I start the Widget Previewer?
faq.answer: Supported IDEs start it automatically. From the project root, the Flutter CLI can start it with the widget-preview command.

faq.question: Can one widget have several previews?
faq.answer: Yes. Apply multiple Preview annotations or use MultiPreview to generate related configurations.

faq.question: Can previews use application themes?
faq.answer: Yes. Configure a theme callback directly or create a custom Preview annotation that applies shared theme data.

faq.question: Why does a widget fail only in the previewer?
faq.answer: The previewer uses a web environment. Native APIs from dart:io, dart:ffi, or dependent plugins can fail there.

faq.question: Do previews replace tests?
faq.answer: No. Previews support rapid visual iteration but do not replace widget, integration, accessibility, or device testing.
